ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: At the Kazan World Swimming Championships in July 2015, our province's famous athlete Chen Ruolin bravely won the women's 10-meter platform championship. She jumped obliquely upward from the platform and, after a period of time, fell into the water, as shown in the figure. Air resistance is not considered. During the process of entering the water, what is the relationship between the magnitude of the force exerted on her by the water and the magnitude of the force exerted by her on the water?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: During the process of entering the water, the magnitude of the force exerted on her by the water is equal to the magnitude of the force exerted by her on the water
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, a diving athlete is above the swimming pool/near the water surface in an inverted, inclined posture, with the body entering toward the water surface, indicating that the athlete will come into contact with the water when entering the water. Then reason: The question asks about the relationship between the magnitude of the force exerted on her by the water and the magnitude of the force exerted by her on the water “during the process of entering the water.” When entering the water, the athlete and the water are two objects interacting with each other; the force of the water on the athlete and the force of the athlete on the water form a pair of action force and reaction force. According to Newton's third law, these two forces are always equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Therefore, when only comparing magnitudes, the two are equal. Final answer: During the process of entering the water, the magnitude of the force exerted on her by the water is equal to the magnitude of the force exerted by her on the water.
